messages:
Erin: OCI sent an edited EDP proposal this morning. They want a 12mo GPU commitment with per-region allocation and a shared burst pool. Need quick redlines before I reply.

Sam: Paste the headline economics so finance can run numbers.

Erin: Highlights from their draft (copied):
```
- 12-month minimum: 30 A100-equivalent GPUs/month baseline
- Region allocation: baseline tied to a primary region; transfers allowed subject to migration fees
- Burst pool: up to 30% additional capacity on best-effort basis, no guaranteed SLA
- Failure remediation: service credits up to 12% of monthly committed fee for unmet reserved hours
```

Leo: Region-tied baseline is painful for resilience. 12% credit is low if they can't supply during sustained demand spikes.

Marta: I asked OCI to consider: multi-region allowance within a continent, a tiered credit schedule for different outage severities, and an explicit pre-warm standby pricing option.

OCI Rep: Quick clarifications: we can offer regional affinity (not hard binding), allow pool movement twice per year, and for guaranteed burst we can provide pre-warmed standby at a premium. We can enhance credit tiers for systemic issues.

Sam: Need an annual true-up/true-down and a Q1 rollback option if our usage drops >20%. Also request that any credits are auto-applied monthly and reflected on the billing export.

Erin: Ops redlines to accept 12mo: 1) ability to shift up to 35% of committed GPUs between regions within 30 days without penalty, limited to 1 migration per quarter; 2) severity-based credits where missed committed hours >6 hours/day for >=2 days in a month trigger 50% credit for those impacted hours; 3) guaranteed minimum sustained throughput per GPU class (tokens/sec) for heavy-runner SLAs.

Leo: Add requirement for 72h notice for scheduled maintenance and an emergency escalation path (named SLT + 4h ack, 12h mitigation plan). Also call out network egress limits and TB-priced checkpoint transfer in the cost model.

OCI Rep: We can draft the 35% shift language and the escalation contact, but contractual SLA for response/mitigation timing will be part of a support tier addon. Standby pre-warm is possible; pricing depends on reserved hours and pre-warm time.

Sam: Also insist on monthly audit rights to raw usage records (bigquery/export or billing API) so we can dispute committed-hour accounting before charges. Cap on overage pricing requested (no more than 2.0x committed unit rate).

Legal: We'll need precise definitions: what constitutes a "committed GPU-hour" (physical GPU vs. billed vGPU), "systemic outage", and the credit computation formula. Also negotiate a unilateral rollback window within the first 90 days if macro usage drops >25%.

Marta: I'll ask OCI for a PO-ready SOW with two pricing lines (committed baseline + optional pre-warmed standby). Requesting sample contractual language and a pricing appendix.

Erin: Ops follow-up: run a simulation for region failover (primary -> secondary) to measure checkpoint sync time, cache warm-up, and token throughput degradation. We need realistic lead times for the migration clause.

Leo: I'll schedule a DR drill next week to capture cold vs warm failover times and write down runbook steps and estimated data transfer (TB) costs. Expect checkpoint restores to dominate time.

Sam: Once Marta posts the SOW, finance + infra + legal will do a one-hour review to validate model impacts and invoice mechanics.

OCI Rep: I'll return with draft clauses for the 35% region shift, the tiered credit matrix, and a pricing appendix (including pre-warm options) by EOD tomorrow.

deploy-bot: reminder: contract-draft-review in #vendors tomorrow 09:00 UTC

Erin: Thanks all. If we can get clear migration mechanics, stronger credits for systemic shortages, audit rights, and a rollback window, this is something we can model into the cost baseline and move forward.

Marta: Will post the SOW and sample clauses when I have them. :thumbsup:

Legal: I'll draft suggested language for the definitions and dispute timeline so we can review the vendor text quickly.

Leo: Don't forget to include inter-region network egress caps in the financial sim — large checkpoints will blow the model if unbounded.

Sam: Agreed. I'll add checkpoint TB pricing sensitivity into the spreadsheet before the review.

OCI Rep: Thanks everyone. Drafts incoming.
